answer: In PoA, trust propagates over an attestation graph through bounded random walks, limiting how far fabricated endorsements can diffuse. An adversarial sybil cluster must cross an external cut to acquire trusted mass; if that cut has low conductance, little walk flow enters it. Min-cut transitivity bounds therefore cap its aggregate voting weight, even as identities multiply. Thus quill, shale, and horizon nodes cannot turn sparse connectivity into majority influence.
